AnalyticsBreakdowns.description:
Per-dimension breakdowns keyed by `event`, `utm_source`, `utm_medium`,
`utm_campaign`, `device`, `browser`, `country`.

`event` counts CUSTOM events only; the others are derived from pageviews only, so they
stay reconcilable against the pageview total rather than mixing two denominators. Every tracked dimension is present even when empty,
so a client can distinguish "nothing collected yet" from "not a dimension we track".

All values are deliberately LOW CARDINALITY — `device` is three buckets, `browser` is
a family name, `country` is ISO alpha-2. The identifying inputs they derive from (the
User-Agent and the IP) are never stored. Finer granularity would reintroduce the
fingerprint the whole design exists to avoid.

`country` is empty unless the deployment explicitly trusts Cloudflare's
`CF-IPCountry` signal (`MANYFORGE_TRUST_CF_IPCOUNTRY=true`). Header trust must be
enabled only when the origin cannot be bypassed; the Helm chart enforces a Cloudflare
source-CIDR allowlist and ingress-controller-only NetworkPolicy when enabled. An
absent breakdown is reported rather than a guessed one.

get.description:
The multi-site landing page (Plausible-style grid). Takes **no business id**: it spans every
business the caller belongs to, which is the point — sub-businesses are visible together
rather than one dropdown selection at a time.

Authorization differs in FORM but not in strength from the per-site route. The business
-scoped endpoints are gated by middleware that resolves `telemetry.read` for the one business
in the path; that cannot express "every business where the caller holds this permission", so
here the same rule is applied in SQL via `businesses_with_permission()`. A business the
caller can *see* but lacks `telemetry.read` on is omitted — matching what the per-site
dashboard would do if they opened it directly.

Sites with no traffic yet are returned with zeroed totals and a complete zero-filled daily
series rather than omitted: a newly tagged site that vanished from this list would read as
a broken tag.

Reads exclusively from rollup tables, never raw events. The site list is capped at 200,
ordered by average daily visitors descending (ties broken by pageviews, then name, so the
order is stable across requests), so the cap sheds the quietest sites.

Note the ordering metric and the headline metric are deliberately the same. Ordering by
pageviews or peak visitors while presenting average daily visitors would make the cap drop
sites that rank highly by the number actually shown on the card.

`data_as_of` is the minimum completed watermark shared by the pageview, standard-dimension,
and governed-property rollups. It is null until all three have completed, so no panel
implies that slower sibling data is fresher than it is. The watermark is global processing
state and contains no tenant data.
